baseline_models.focus_anchor: خُذُوهُ فَغُلُّوهُ: two imperatives share the same object pronoun, with fa making restraint follow seizure.
baseline_models.mechanism: Capture removes the person from free custody; the following collar fixes the captured body in durable incapacity.

activation_trace.role: Capture and captivity supplies the literal transfer of the person into custody.
A collar binding a limb supplies the literal durable restraint that completes the seizure.

changed_reading.before: Two adjacent punishment orders: take him and bind him.
changed_reading.after: A two-stage custody operation: acquire bodily control, then convert it into stable incapacitation.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The imperative خُذُوهُ can carry taking-to-account, while فَغُلُّوهُ fastens the same pronominal object.
baseline_models.mechanism: A fault first makes the person liable to being taken; the shackle then turns that liability from an abstract obligation into a condition borne by the body.

activation_trace.role: Taking someone to account for a fault supplies the juridical force inside the first imperative.
The binding collar, including restraint or obligation in its scope, makes liability bodily and inescapable.

changed_reading.before: An arrest followed by an unexplained shackle.
changed_reading.after: Taking-to-account culminates in liability physically fastened onto the accountable person.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence moves from خُذُوهُ, gaining possession, to غُلُّوهُ, whose root inventory includes fixed insertion through gaps.
baseline_models.mechanism: The commands progressively close escape: first possession of the whole person, then an interlocking restraint that occupies the available openings and fixes him within it.

activation_trace.role: Taking into hand or possession supplies the first, whole-body acquisition stage.
Stable insertion through interstices supplies a more invasive second stage of fixing, beyond mere contact.

changed_reading.before: Seize him, then attach a restraint.
changed_reading.after: Possession tightens into interlocking incorporation, a progression from external control toward being fixed inside a restraining arrangement.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context first makes a human the recipient and exhibitor of a written object, then the focus reverses the relation: the failed recipient is himself the object denoted by -hu, taken for further processing.

activation_trace.role: Taking into possession anchors the focus person's new status as the handled object.
Giving supplies the earlier transfer in which the person receives, rather than becomes, the transferred object.
A written record that establishes an obligating judgment makes the received book consequential rather than inert.
Reading and recitation supplies the successful scene's human agency over the displayed record.

structural_cues: 69:19 gives the person a book and lets him call for its reading; 69:25 repeats the passive giving but adds a wish not to have received it; 69:30 makes the person the repeated pronominal object.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two transfer scenes, a judgment-bearing record, and a shared object pronoun; I infer a reversal of object status. A live alternative is that the passages contrast outcomes without making the person analogous to the book.

changed_reading.before: Enforcers take a condemned person after his failed accounting.
changed_reading.after: The failed receiver and reader of the record is stripped of subject agency and becomes the item handed into custody.

context_deltas.mechanism: Meeting the account produces a decisive judgment while the person's own authority disappears; خُذُوهُ therefore acts as execution of verdict and فَغُلُّوهُ as the visible transfer of governing power over his body.

activation_trace.role: Taking to account for fault makes the seizure juridical rather than merely predatory.
The collar's enforced restraint embodies the resulting obligation and loss of self-command.
What a person encounters of good or evil supplies the awaited encounter as an outcome that arrives upon him.
Counting and account supplies the adjudicative operation whose result the custody enforces.
A decisive judgment supplies the terminal character of the wished-for but unavailable resolution.
Power and governing authority, explicitly lost in the verse, supplies the control that passes to the executors.

structural_cues: 69:20 anticipates meeting an account; 69:26 denies prior knowledge; 69:27 wishes for finality; 69:28-29 repeat loss from the first-person center immediately before the command.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies account, decisive closure, vanished authority, and then seizure; I infer that the imperatives execute a verdict and transfer jurisdiction. They may alternatively be only chronological penalties following judgment.

changed_reading.before: Accountability explains why punishment occurs before an ordinary arrest.
changed_reading.after: The arrest is itself the verdict becoming operative: authority leaves the judged speaker and is fastened over his body.

context_deltas.mechanism: A positive command to eat and drink is inverted by failed feeding and exclusive punitive food; the focus root's images of inward entry and unquenched heat let the shackle mark a transition from choosing intake to having appetite and interiority placed under custody.

activation_trace.role: Stable inward entry, including food or drink entering the belly in the branch scope, anchors an interior dimension of the binding.
Heat and unquenched thirst lodged in the belly supplies the captive appetite that persists beneath the physical collar.
Freely taking liquid supplies the earlier, pleasant mode of intake that the focus sequence reverses.
Feeding another supplies the social circulation of nourishment that the condemned person failed even to urge.
Heat and severity associated with غسلين supplies an afflictive replacement for pleasant intake.
Eating supplies the terminal action now restricted to the culpable class rather than offered as a gift.

structural_cues: 69:24 commands plural beneficiaries to eat and drink pleasantly; 69:34 names the failure to urge feeding; 69:36-37 restrict food and eaters after the singular body has been seized.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a consumption arc and focus branches of inward entry and thirst; I infer that shackling mediates loss of alimentary agency. A live alternative is that food imagery merely surrounds an exclusively external restraint.

changed_reading.before: The shackle controls locomotion before later food punishment.
changed_reading.after: The shackle also marks captivity of intake: the eater's interior becomes governed, heated, and supplied on punitive terms.

context_deltas.mechanism: The shackle is not the endpoint of immobilization but a staging interface: connected links receive the captive, and insertion routes him through a larger restraining system.

activation_trace.role: Capture supplies the acquisition of the body that can then be positioned and routed.
Fixed insertion through gaps supplies the mechanical hinge between initial restraint and later threading.
Connected rings and parts supply the extended structure into which the local shackle is integrated.
Inserting one thing into another supplies the explicit routing action that completes the focus root's latent insertion image.

structural_cues: The repeated ثم orders shackle, fire, and insertion; the same masculine object remains under command through 69:30-32, and the chain receives an explicit measure.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies ordered stages, connected rings, insertion, and a persistent object; I infer that the first shackle prepares alignment with the larger chain. The live alternative is a list of cumulative but mechanically independent penalties.

changed_reading.before: The second imperative simply immobilizes the captive.
changed_reading.after: It docks the captive into a punishment pipeline, preparing his body to be threaded through an extended connected apparatus.

context_deltas.mechanism: The stated offenses are failures of inward assent and outward social urging; because the shackle branch also spans restraint and miserliness, the punishment can mirror those closures: one who did not let trust settle or nourishment circulate is now himself withheld from free movement.

activation_trace.role: Taking to account for fault anchors the reciprocal mechanism as liability, not free symbolism.
The literal collar and the branch scope's metaphorical restraint or miserliness supply the hinge from social withholding to bodily withholding.
Assent that brings the heart to rest supplies the inward reception explicitly negated in the causal account.
Urging toward an act supplies the social propulsion that the person refused to generate.
Feeding another supplies the outward provision whose circulation should have been encouraged.

structural_cues: إنه كان and the following coordinated negatives present lack of faith and lack of urging food as grounds after the command sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies explicit grounds plus branch images of settled assent, urging, feeding, and restraint; I supply the reciprocal arrow from withheld circulation to bodily withholding. The offenses may instead justify punishment without shaping its form.

changed_reading.before: The body is restrained as a generic penalty for two independent offenses.
changed_reading.after: The restraint can be an embodied return of closure: refused inward and social circulation reappears as the offender's own arrested movement.

context_deltas.mechanism: Explicit absence of any close relation removes a possible counterclaim on the captive; taking into possession thus becomes not only arrest but forced transfer from human belonging into unopposed hostile custody.

activation_trace.role: Taking into hand or possession supplies the new custodial claim over the person.
Capture and captivity makes that claim coercive rather than protective.
The binding collar makes hostile custody durable after no relation intervenes.
Denial of the present state supplies the categorical removal of available support here and now.
Close kinship and intimate relation supplies the protective bond whose absence leaves custody uncontested.

structural_cues: The possessive له, temporal اليوم, and locative هاهنا make the missing intimate a relation unavailable to him at the punishment site.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies coercive possession followed by categorical absence of a close relation; I infer replacement of belonging by hostile custody. Alternatively, the absent intimate may describe isolation without functioning as a failed counterclaim.

changed_reading.before: Capture isolates the person because shackles prevent escape.
changed_reading.after: Capture replaces relational belonging: with no close claimant here, punitive possession of the person becomes total and uncontested.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the imperative most directly orders a physical shackle. It remains anchored in the focus roots' bodily seizure and hidden-rancor branches and in the following negation of heart-settling assent; render it only as a symbolic interior echo, not as a replacement for the collar sense.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: خُذُوهُ can image a condition taking hold in a body, while غُلُّوهُ shares a root with rancor lodged unseen in the chest.

activation_trace.role: A condition taking hold in the body supplies an inward seizure that can precede external custody.
Rancor hidden in the chest supplies a latent inner binding that the iron collar may externalize.
Heart-rest in security and trust, here negated, supplies the contrasting interior state that failed to displace closure.

changed_reading.before: Iron restraint arrives wholly from outside after judgment.
changed_reading.after: The external collar may materialize an inward capture already lodged in the person's affective and believing life.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This cross-domain reading is surprising because a chain is not literally a text or register. It stays valid as an analogy anchored in the focus root's fixed insertion, the judgment-bearing book, connected links, and explicit insertion; downstream prose should call it a materialized-record effect, not a lexical equation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: فَغُلُّوهُ fixes the same person who was entered in a consequential book scene and is next inserted into linked material.

activation_trace.role: Stable insertion and fixation supplies the focus-level act that can become bodily inscription.
Entering a name into a register or group supplies the documentary pattern later recast in material form.
Connected rings supply a material sequence analogous to joined entries or signs.
Insertion of one thing into another supplies the act by which the judged body becomes an element inside that sequence.

changed_reading.before: The book records judgment, and the chain separately enforces it.
changed_reading.after: Enforcement can look like bodily inscription: the judged person is fixed as an entry inside a linked material register.

strongest_changes: The paired imperatives became a custody pipeline: capture, durable restraint, then routing into a connected chain.
The book and account scenes reverse objecthood: a receiver and would-be reader becomes the object taken and processed.
The stated failures activate a reciprocal social reading in which refused assent and nourishment-circulation return as bodily restraint.
The eating and drinking frame preserves an exploratory inward reading in which captivity reaches appetite, thirst, and intake.
summary.what_was_special: The same two-word focus sustained juridical, mechanical, social, relational, and metabolic mechanisms without forcing them into one final sense; the strongest surprise was that taking changes the person's grammatical and proprietary status, while shackling can function as both verdict and routing interface.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether the interior-entry and thirst branches of غ ل ل should color this imperative beyond the primary collar branch.
Whether object reversal and bodily inscription are designed structural effects or reader-supplied analogies produced by adjacency.
How strongly failure to urge feeding supports reciprocal withholding rather than merely naming an independent ground for punishment.
